successors.name: Kingdom of Mercia
successors.text: 'In 771, King Offa of Mercia conquered the territory of the Haestingas', and 'By 772 he apparently controlled the whole of the Kingdom of Sussex'

ledger.x: 477: Ælle and his three sons land and found the South Saxon kingdom.
491: Ælle takes the Saxon Shore fort of Andredadsceaster (Pevensey).
661: Wulfhere of Mercia gives Æthelwealh the Meonwara.
661: the Isle of Wight is given to Sussex.
686: Cædwalla of Wessex conquers the Isle of Wight.

c. 686: Sussex falls under West Saxon rule. Infobox 'Subject to Wessex: c. 686 to c. 715'; Cædwalla killed Æthelwealh, was expelled by the ealdormen Berhthun and Andhun, and 'Once on the throne, Cædwalla attacked the South Saxons again, this time killing Berthun'. The vassal's record: the…
c. 715: Sussex shakes off Wessex. Infobox 'Subject to Wessex: c. 686 to c. 715'; 'In 710 Sussex was still under West Saxon domination' and Sussex broke away 'some time before 722'.
771: Offa of Mercia conquers the Haestingas.

wars.name: West Saxon-South Saxon fighting of 607
wars.outcome: The page records only 'when Ceolwulf of Wessex fought against the South Saxons'; no land is said to change hands.

wars.name: West Saxon campaign against Sussex (725)
wars.outcome: The Chronicle 'records a further West Saxon campaign in 725'; the page gives no outcome and Sussex is not recorded as subject again.

wars.name: Offa's conquest of Sussex
wars.outcome: Offa conquered the Haestingas in 771 and 'By 772 he apparently controlled the whole of the Kingdom of Sussex'; Sussex was 'subject to Mercia' from 771 to c.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line on any page opened: the frontier with Kent, Surrey and Hampshire is the later county line taken as approximate; the Meon valley edge is the least certain.
